cells.tense: You are here in the moment, shifting what you do as you feel it.
cells.ask: Tell one person the small true thing you noticed about a room you're standing in, in your own words, today.
cells.core:
You notice the room and you move with it. Someone says less than they mean and you feel it before you name it; you shift how you say the next thing and the conversation keeps breathing. That's not guessing ahead. It's you, here, doing it as it happens.

Going well, this looks like being moved without losing your feet. The feeling comes, you follow where it actually leads, and you don't need to settle on what it means first. There's a cost to keeping it live: you stay in the question instead of closing it early, and some days that's work. Direction here comes from being genuinely in the room. You're not managing the moment. You're meeting it.

cells.tense: You are getting yourself ready for a moment that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.ask: Let one thing today go exactly as it lands — say nothing, fix nothing, watch what it does.
cells.core:
You've got the next version of this running ahead of you. You read the mood before anyone speaks, decide in advance how you'll hold yourself, land on the right way to say it before the conversation happens — and then you're mostly attending to the plan instead of the person. The moment you prepared for isn't the one you're in.

When this is working, care doesn't have to exhaust anything: you hold what's here without clutching at what's next, and direction comes from what actually shows up. So let one thing land unmanaged. Not the whole day — one thing. You'll still be you in the room. Just not a step in front of it.

cells.tense: The moment is in front of you, but you are standing outside it.
cells.ask: Ask one person how their week actually went, and let the whole answer finish without repairing any of it.
cells.core:
Things come toward you and you let them pass at a little distance. You can still follow a conversation, still see what's going on — and you're watching it rather than in it, giving nothing back that would change the shape of it.

What's thin here isn't the ability to feel. It's showing up with it. This doesn't get fixed by trying harder to feel or pushing feeling into a spot that's run dry — it comes back sideways, through plain curiosity. Ask someone a real question. Listen to all of it, including the parts that make you want to fix things. Let their answer land in you and rearrange something. That's the way back in.

cells.tense: You are already catching what's under the surface and shifting with what you find.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once today, the thing you picked up from a room you were in — just what you noticed, nothing built on it.
cells.core:
It runs the whole time. A tone shifts and you adjust your own before you've decided to; you walk in somewhere and within a minute you have a read on what the place is carrying. You call this being reasonable, or going along with things, or just knowing how people are.

When it's working, catching things is a practice rather than a worry — time alone keeps you connected instead of closed, and refining what you notice sharpens what you're making rather than what you're dreading. So put your own name on one instance of it. You caught something. You moved. That's a real thing you did, and nobody made you do it.

attempts.check: One claim the record doesn't support: that the person is reading under other people's surfaces — the kernel says imagination-as-behavior through resonance, and my Unacknowledged cell leans on mind-reading other people, which the record never states. The reader could fairly say 'I don't do that, I just don't say much.' The ask still works if I'm wrong: saying one thing you noticed out loud teaches something whether or not it's already running as a habit. The sentence that serves me more than them: 'nobody made you do it' — it's an argument, not a reading, and it flatters the frame I built. Fixed by grounding status 4 in the person's own impressions, not other people's hidden states, and by un-nouning the verb.
